resources.title: Arabic Alphabets #1
resources.description: Theme: ARABIC ALPHABET | Content: ذ د خ ح ج ث ت ب أ ط ض ص ش س ز ر ن م ل ك ق ف غ ع ظ ي و ـه
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Pronounce the Arabic Alphabets correctly. 2. Identify each of the Alphabets.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Writes the Alphabets boldly on chalkboard. 2. Pronounces the Alphabets and asks the pupils to do so several times. 3. Uses flash card to guide pupils to recognize and identify it. 4. Guides pupils as they write the Alphabets.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher’s pronunciation attentively. 2. Pronounce the Alphabets trying as much as possible to imitate their teacher. 3. Identify the Alphabets.
resources.resources: 1. A cardboard on which the Alphabets are boldly written. 2. Flash Cards. 3. Information Technology Devices.
resources.assessment: Pupils to:- 1. Pronounce the Arabic Alphabets correctly. 2. Identify each of the Alphabets.

resources.title: Arabic Alphabets #2
resources.description: Theme: ARABIC ALPHABET | Content: ذ د خ ح ج ث ت ب أ ط ض ص ش س ز ر ن م ل ك ق ف غ ع ظ ي و ـه
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: Pronounce the simple Arabic Alphabets.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Revises all the alphabets taught. 2. Writes the alphabet on the board one after the other and pronounce them. 3. Asks the pupils to pronounce them and repeat them several times. 4. Points at some of the letters and asks some pupils to pronounce them.

Students: 1. Listen carefully to the teacher’s pronunciation and pronounce the alphabet. 2. Recite the alphabet on their own several times. 3. Identify the alphabets. 4. Write down the Arabic alphabets.
resources.resources: 1. A cardboard on which the Alphabets are boldly written. 2. Flash Card.
resources.assessment: Pupils to:- Pronounce the Alphabets correctly.

resources.title: Arabic Alphabets #3
resources.description: Theme: ARABIC ALPHABET | Content: ذ د خ ح ج ث ت ب أ ط ض ص ش س ز ر ن م ل ك ق ف غ ع ظ ي و ـه
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: Pronounce the Arabic Alphabets correctly.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Revises the previous alphabets. 2. Writes the complex alphabet on the board one after the other and pronounces them. 3. Asks the pupils to pronounce them. 4. Points at some of the letters and asks some pupils to pronounce them. 5. Recites all the (28) alphabets together and asks the pupils to recite them.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher and pronounce the letter the way he does. 2. Pay special attention to letters with similar sounds. 3. Recite all the letters and trying to identify them individually. 4. Write down the Arabic alphabets.
resources.resources: A cardboard on which the Alphabets are boldly written.
resources.assessment: Pupils to:- Pronounce the alphabets correctly.

resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Recite Suratul – Fātiha correctly. 2. Memorize Suratul – Fātiha. 3. Mention the circumstances that one can read the Surah.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Recites Suratul – F ā t i h a s l o w l y w o r d by word. 2. Asks the pupils to recite it the way he does. 3. Pinpoints the difficult words and pronounces them verse by verse. 4. Recites the Surah aayah by aayah and asks pupils to recite it several times. 5. Tells them the times when the Surah can be recited.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher’s recitation attentively. 2. Recite after the teacher collectively. 3. Recite after the teacher individually. 4. Recite the Surah several times to give room for memorization.

resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Recite Suratul- Fātiha correctly. 2. Mention the time that one can read the Surah.

Teacher: 1. Revises Suratul- Fatiha previously taught to them. 2. Recites the new Surah slowly and asks pupils to recite it. 3. Students: 1. Listen to the teacher and recite the Surah after him. 2. Recite the Surah several times to give room for memorization. 3. Recite after the teacher collectively. 4. Recite after the teacher individually.

resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Revises Suratun- Nas taught in the previous lesson. 2. Recites Suratul – Falaq slowly and asks pupils to recite. 3. Points at the difficult words, pronounces them and ask the pupils to do the same. 4. Asks them to recite it several times. 5. Tells them the times to recite the Surah.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher and recite the Surah the way he does. 2. Recite the Surah several times for easier memorization. 3. Recite after the teacher collectively. 4. Recite after the teacher individually.
resources.resources: 1. A copy of the Glorious Qur’an. 2. Recorded Cassettes, CD, MP etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Recite Suratul - Falaq correctly. 2. Memorize Suratul – Falaq 3. State the times when the Surah may be recited.

resources.title: Suratul - Ikhlas.
resources.description: Theme: QUR’AN AND QUR’ANIC TEXT | Content: The Arabic text of Suratul – Ikhlas. نمحرلا الله مسب ميحرلا ُاللَّه )1( ٌدحَ َأ ُاللَّه وَ هُ لْ ُق مْ َلوَ دْ لَِي مْ َل )2( ُدمَ صه لا ُهَل نْ كُ َي مْ َلوَ )3( دْ َلوُي )4( ٌدحَ َأ اوً ُفكُ

resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Revises Surah taught. 2. Recites the new Surah slowly and asks the pupils to recite it. 3. Lays emphasis on difficult words. 4. Recites the Surah several times and a s k s t h e p u p il s to do so. 5. Tells them the times to recite the Surah. 6. Tells them that God is one.

Students: 1. Listen attentively and recite the way the teacher does. 2. Repeat the recitation several times to facilitate memorization. 3. Recite after the teacher collectively. 4. Recite after the teacher individually.
resources.resources: 1. A copy of the Glorious Qur’an. 2. Recorded Cassettes, CD, MP etc. of the Surah.

resources.title: Articles of faith in Islam
resources.description: Theme: TAWHID | Content: 1. Belief in Allah. 2. Belief in His Prophet. 3. Belief in His Angels. 4. Belief in the Revealed Books. 5. Belief in the day of judgement 6. Belief in the pre- destination, good and bad.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Enumerate the articles of faith in Islam. 2. Memorize the six articles of faith in Islam.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Enumerates the six articles of faith in Islam. 2. Explains the articles of faith in Islam briefly. 3. Outlines the importance of articles of faith in Islam.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the teacher. 2. Read the Articles collectively after the teacher and individually. 3. Read the Articles of faith several times.
resources.resources: Cardboard showing the Articles of faith.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Enumerate six articles of faith in Islam. 2. Mention the Articles in Arabic.

resources.title: Four of the attributes of Allah
resources.description: Theme: TAWHID | Content: قلاخلا 1. Al- Kahaliq برلا 2. Ar- Rabb 3. Ar- Rahman نمحرلا ميحرلا 4. Ar- Rahim
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Enumerate four among the attribute of Allah 2. Mention the Arabic names for these attributes.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Tell the pupils the Arabic words for attributes 2. Pronounces the Arabic names one after the other and asks the pupils to pronounce them. 3. Explains that these attributes are peculiar to the Al- mighty Allah alone and points briefly at their peculiarities. 4. Guides pupils’ direction on the attributes of Allah.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the teacher. 2. Pronounce the attributes after the teacher collectively and individually. 3. Pronounce the Arabic names for the four attributes several times.
resources.resources: Cardboard showing the four attributes of Allah.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Enumerate four among the attribute of Allah. 2. Mention the Arabic names for these attributes.

resources.title: Allah the only Creator (Al-Khaliq)
resources.description: Theme: TAWHID | Content: 1. Differences between man- made products and Allah’s creatures. 2. Man’s inability to create living things.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Differentiate between man- made products and Allah’s creatures. 2. State why man cannot create things that have life.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Asks pupils to gather various toys, gives examples of living things and discusses them. 2. Explains that existing materials, from which toys and models were made, were created by Allah. 3. Points out that man cannot give life to their toys. 4. Enlightens pupils on the differences between Allah’s creation and things made by man.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the teacher. 2. Pronounce the attributes after the teacher collectively and individually. 3. Pronounce the Arabic names for the four attributes several times.
resources.resources: Cardboard showing the four attributes of Allah.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Differentiate between man- made products and Allah’s creatures. 2. State why man cannot create things that have life.

resources.title: Allah the sustainer (Ar-Rabb)
resources.description: Theme: TAWHID | Content: Essential things provided by Allah to sustain the creatures: - Air, water, light, heat, food, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Give examples of essential things provided by Allah to sustain the creatures. 2. State that Allah is the sustainer of all the creatures.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the values of these essential things. 2. Asks pupils to observe the growth and conditions of the seeds earlier planted under different conditions.

Students: 1. Observe and take note of the differences in growth and conditions of these seeds planted under different conditions. 2. Observe that water, air, light etc are very essential for the survival and sustenance of all living things. 3. Conclude that Allah is the sustainer of all living things (Ar-Rabb).
resources.resources: 1. Seeds, seedlings, pots or tins, water, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Give examples of essential things provided by Allah to sustain the creatures. 2. State that Allah is the sustainer of all the creatures.

resources.title: Allah the Beneficent (Ar- Rahman) and the Merciful (Ar-Rahim)
resources.description: Theme: TAWHID | Content: Allah as the Beneficent (Ar-Rahman) نمحرلا and the Merciful (Ar-Rahim) ميحرلا
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Give examples of Allah’s mercies to all His creatures. 2. Explain that Islam is also a mercy of Allah to all Human beings.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Revises with pupils the previous lessons on Allah, the sustainer. 2. Explains the meaning of Allah’s beneficence and mercy by pointing out that rain, sun, moon, air etc are some of His blessings. 3. Explains that Islam is also a mercy from Allah because it directs people to the right path. 4. Asks them to mention few other things that are parts of Allah’s blessings upon the creature.

Students: 1. Listen and follow the teacher’s explanations. 2. Think of some other things provided by Allah as a kind of His beneficence and mercy and mention them.
resources.resources: Pictures of the sun, the moon, the stars, rivers etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Give some examples of Allah’s mercies to all His creatures. 2. Explain that Islam is also a mercy from Allah to all Human beings.

resources.title: Cleanliness in Islam (Taharah).
resources.description: Theme: FIQH | Content: i. Cleanliness as part of teaching in Islam. ii. How cleanliness is practised iii. Advantages of cleanliness.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Explain the need for cleanliness in their daily lives. 2. Demonstrate the ways cleanliness can be practised. 3. Enumerate the advantages of cleanliness.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads pupils through discussion to realize the need for cleanliness. 2. Explains that cleanliness is part of the teaching of Islam, 3. Uses relevant Hadith and ayahs of the Qur’an. 4. Tells pupils that ablution, toilet habits etc are part of the teaching of Islam. 5. Explains different ways of cleaning the body, the clothes, food, surrounding etc. 6. Tells them how to realize the advantages of cleanliness.

Students: 1. Listen carefully to the teacher’s discussion and follow the points being made. 2. Practise the various forms of cleanliness in Islam. 3. Discuss some disadvantages of un- cleanliness and untidiness. 4. Describe some of the things we use for cleanliness.
resources.resources: Pictures showing the means of cleanliness: Water, soap and broom etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Explain the need for cleanliness in their daily lives. 2. Demonstrate the ways cleanliness can be practised. 3. Enumerate the advantages of cleanliness.

resources.title: How to perform Al-Wudu’
resources.description: Theme: FIQH | Content: 1. Al-wudu’ 2. Why and how it is performed. 3. What is required for performing Al-wudu’
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. State what Al- wudu’ is. 2. Explain the purpose of Al- wudu’ 3. Demonstrate how to perform Al- wudu’
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains to pupils why Al-wudu’ is performed. 2. Demonstrates how it is performed asking the pupils to imitate him step by step. 3. Takes the pupils out of the classroom for practical Al-wudu’. 4. Ask pupils to demonstrate Al-wudu’ in turns.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher and watch all the procedure. 2. Bring items used for performing wudu’ to the class. 3. Demonstrate how to perform Al- wudu’
resources.resources: 1. A clean kettle of pure water. 2. Hand washing basin. 3. Pictures showing different stages of ablution.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. State what Al- wudu’ is. 2. Explain the purpose of Al- wudu’. 3. Demonstrate how to perform Al-wudu’.

resources.title: Things that spoil Al-wudu’
resources.description: Theme: FIQH | Content: The things that spoil Al-wudu’ 1. Stool 2. Passing wind 3. Passing urine 4. Deep Sleep etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: Enumerate the things that spoil Al-wudu’
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Asks pupils to explain how wudu’ is performed. 2. Explains the things that spoil ablution as stated under the content. 3. Tells them that when Al-wudu’ is spoilt, one cannot perform salaat unless fresh Al-wudu’ performed.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher’s explanations for better understanding. 2. Learn by heart the things that spoil al-wudu’.
resources.resources: Pictures showing people while urinating or sleeping.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: Enumerate the things that spoil Al- wudu’

resources.title: The five daily Salaats
resources.description: Theme: FIQH | Content: 1. Names of the five daily salaats: Subhi, Zuhr, Asr, Magrib and Isha’i. 2. Times of these salaats. 3. Description of the number of raka’ah for each prayer.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Mention the names of the five daily salaats. 2. State the times of these salats. 3. Mention the number of raka’ah for each prayer. [ 4. Mention that salaat is an act of obedience to Allah
resources.activities:
Teacher: The teacher: - 1. Explains the need for salaat and mentions the names of the five daily slat as indicated under the content. 2. Tells the pupils the time of each prayers as well as the number of raka’h it contains. 3. Takes the pupils out of the classroom to demonstrate various stages of a raka’h. 4. Calls out pupils in turns to demonstrate as well. 5. Explains that prayer is an act of obedience to Allah.

Students: The pupils: - 1. Listen to the teacher’s explanations. 2. Pronounce the names of the salaats. 3. Pay special attention to the time of each salaat and the number of raka’t it contains 4. Observe the teacher closely while demonstrating the salaats. 5. Demonstrate how to perform a raka’ah. 6. Mention that prayer is an act of obedience to Allah.
resources.resources: 1. Mats or carpets, bowl of pure water. 2. Pictures of a person performing various stages of raka’ah.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Mention the names of the five daily salaats. 2. State times of these salaats. 3. Describe the various stages of a raka’ah. 4. Mention the importance of salaats.

resources.title: Al-Adhan
resources.description: Theme: FIQH | Content: 1. The text of Al-Adhan. 2. The time of Al-Adhan. 3. The reason why Al-Adhan is said.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Recite the text of Al-Adhan. 2. State the time Al-Adhan is said. 3. Explain why Al-Adhan is said.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Revises with the pupils how salaat is performed. 2. Recites the text of Al- Adhan and asks pupils to recite it after him. 3. Repeats this action several times. 4. Tells the pupils that Al-Adhan is said few minutes before every obligatory salaat. 5. Explains that the purpose of Al-Adhan is to alert Muslims and invite to the congregational salaat.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher’s explanation on how Al-Adhan is said. 2. Recite the text of Al-Adhan after the teacher. 3. Repeat this several times.
resources.resources: 1. Picture of a person reciting Al-Adhan. 2. Recorded cassette, video cassette, CD, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Recite Al- Adhan. 2. State the time when Al-Adhan is to be said. 3. Guide reasons why Adhan is said.

resources.title: Prophet Muhammad as the last prophet and messenger of Allah.
resources.description: Theme: SIRAH | Content: 1. Prophet Muhammad (the seal of all the prophets). 2. International nature of his message. 3. The Glorious Qur’an as the final guidance of Allah.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. State that he was sent to the whole world. 2. Explain that the Glorious Qur’an was sent to him as the final guidance of Allah to mankind.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains to the pupils who the Prophet Muhammad was pointing out that he was the seal of all the prophets. 2. Tells them that his message is international in nature because it is meant for the whole world. 3. Informs them that the Glorious Qur’an, which was sent through Prophet Muhammad (SAW), was the final guidance of Allah to mankind.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher attentively and follow the discussions point by point.
resources.resources: 1. A copy of the Glorious Qur’ān. 2. Chalk board, slate etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to:- State that Prophet Muhammad was the seal of all the prophets.

resources.title: Names of the first five Prophets of Allah as mentioned in the Glorious Qur’an
resources.description: Theme: SIRAH | Content: Names: Adam, Nuh, Hud, Salih and Lut. Their messages: 1. Commanding what is good. 2. Forbidding what is evil e.g. Qur’ān103 vs 1-3.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Mention the names of the first five Prophets of Allah. 2. State the contents of their messages.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Writes the names of the Prophets on the chalkboard one after the other and pronounce them. 2. Asks the pupils to pronounce the names as well. 3. Asks them to repeat these names several times. 4. Explains to them that the messages of these Prophets comprise two things namely: (i) Commanding good (ii) Forbidding evil with examples 5. Asks them to repeat these two aspects several times. 6. Asks them to point at their mates who bear the Prophets’ names.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher and pronounce the names the way he does. 2. Repeat the names several times. 3. Pay special attention to two segments of the Prophet’s messages for proper understanding. 4. Look around the class and point at their mates who bear the Prophets’ names as may be required by the teacher. 5. List some good and evil deeds.
resources.resources: Cardboard showing the names of the Prophets.
resources.assessment: Pupils to:- 1. Mention the names of the first five Prophets of Allah. 2. State the contents of their messages.

resources.title: Obedience to Allah.
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB | Content: 1. Obedience to Allah. 2. Various ways of Allah’s blessing on the creatures 3. Ways of showing obedience to Allah.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Explain the reason why they should be obedient to Allah 2. Explain the ways in which Allah shows His kindness and favours to His creatures. 3. State the ways people should show their obedience to Allah.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains to the pupils the need to obey Allah because of His blessings. 2. Takes the pupils outside the classroom to observe natural objects like the sun, flowers, trees, birds etc. 3. Explains to them that all these creatures are for the benefit of human beings indicating His kindness to them. 4. Points out that we should obey Him by worshipping Him and following His guidance. 5. Asks them to mention other things Allah has created for the benefit of human beings.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the teacher’s explanation. 2. Observe the natural objects very well and realize through them the need to obey Allah. 3. Mention some benefits you derive from Allah’s creatures.
resources.assessment: Pupi1ls ton: 1. Explain the ways in which Allah shows His kindness and favours to His creatures. 2. State the ways people should show their obedience to Allah.

resources.title: Obedience to Parents
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB | Content: 1. Obedience to parents. 2. Reasons for it and the ways it can be shown.Q17: 23
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Explain the reasons why they should obey their parents. 2. State ways in which they can obey their parents.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains positive roles played by the parents in their children up bringing justifying the need to obey them. 2. Discusses the way through which obedience can be shown to them i.e. love them, be kind to them, greet them in the mourning do things that will make them happy.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher’s explanation. 2. Think of any other ways by which the parents can be obeyed and mention them. 3. Dramatize ways in which one can show disobedience to his parents. 4. Practice exchange of greetings in the class. 5. Demonstrate eating manners before the class.
resources.resources: 1. The glorious Qur’an. 2. Information Technology Device.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Explain reasons why they should respect their parents and teachers. 2. Explain the ways in which they can respect their parents and teachers;

resources.title: Islamic Rules of Conduct.
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB | Content: 1. Islamic rules of conduct relating to: Table manners, sneezing and greetings. 2. The reasons why Islamic rules of conduct should be observed. 3. Types of greetings.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Demonstrate Islamic rules of conduct relating to: (i) table manners (ii) sneezing (iii) greetings etc. 2. State the reasons why Islamic rules of conduct should be observed. 3. State why greetings are important in Islam.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads pupils to act how to take a meal from the beginning to the end. 2. Tells the pupils what to say at the beginning of a meal i.e, Bismillah , and at the end of a meal Al-hamudulilah. 3. Guides pupils to things to do when eating alone or with others e.g. eating from ones side, avoiding eating greedily or talking while eating etc. 4. Explains types of greetings to the pupils.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher attentively. 2. Observe the teacher’s demonstration with keen interest and practice accordingly. 3. Pronounce the dua’u to be said by a sneezer and the responses to be given. 4. Take note of Islamic rules of conducts relating to greetings and practise it accordingly. 5. Exchange of the greetings in the class. 6. Demonstrate eating manner before the class.
resources.resources: Pictures showing different Islamic rules of conduct relating to eating, sneezing and greetings.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: Demonstrate different ways of conduct in eating, sneezing and greetings etc.

resources.title: Revision of Arabic Alphabets
resources.description: Theme: QUR’AN AND QUR’ANIC TEXT | Content: 1. Recognition of the alphabets. 2. Pronunciation of the various alphabets.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Read the Arabic alphabets correctly. 2. Identify the alphabets.
resources.activities:
Teacher: Revises the alphabets.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the teacher’s recitation. 2. Repeat the surah after the teacher. 3. Recite the surah in group and individually. 4. Repeat the mispronounced words after the teacher. 5. Recite the surah off hand.

resources.title: Asmau- lahilhusna (No 11-20)
resources.description: Theme: TAWHID | Content: Al-Mutakabhir (The Majesty) ربكتملا Al-Khaliq (The Creator) قلاخلا Al-Barr (The Evolver) ربلا Musawwir (The Fashioner) رّوصملا Al-Ghaffar (The Forgiver) رافّ غلا Al-Qahar (The Subduer) راهقلا Al-Wahab (The Bestower) باهّ ولا Fattah (The Opener) حاّتفلا Ar-Razzaq (The Enricher) قازرلا Al-Alim (The All Knowing) ميلعلا
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Recite the ten names of Allah listed under content. 2. Read the meaning of these names in English. 3. Commit the names to memory.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Writes the ten names of Allah as listed under content in Arabic on the chalkboard, or come with the list on cardboard to the class. 2. Writes the English meaning of each name against its Arabic text. 3. Explains the meaning and importance of each. 4. Guides pupils through repeated recitation to learn them by heart.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to how each name is pronounced. 2. Recite the names after the teacher. 3. Recite the names individually or in-group. 4. Repeatedly recite the names to memorize them.
resources.resources: 1. Cardboard on which the names were written in Arabic with their English meanings. 2. An audio clip of the names in cassette, CD, MP etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Recite the ten asmaulahilh- usna listed under content. 2. Read the meanings of these names in English. 3. Commit the names to memory.

resources.title: Belief in Angels.
resources.description: Theme: TAWHID | Content: 1. Angels are creatures of Allah made up of light. Some of the Angels are Jibril, Mikai’l, Ridwan, Atid, Malak al- Maut, Munkar, Nakir and Israfil. 2. Their functions and specific duties e.g. carrying messages to Prophets and Messengers of Allah, discharging other duties as may be assigned to them by Allah, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Explain that Angels are creatures of Allah, created from light. 2. Recall the names of the Angels learnt. 3. Point out the specific duties of the Angels.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Mentions the articles of faith. 2. Calls pupils’ attention to belief in Angels. 3. Mentions the names of some Angels. 4. Writes these names on the chalkboard. 5. Explains the major and specific functions or duties of Angels.

Students: 1. Mention the articles of faith. 2. Mention the names of some Angels. 3. Mention their duties.
resources.resources: 1. Chalkboard, flashcard etc. 2. containing the names of the Angels.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Explain that Angels are creatures of Allah, created from light. 2. Recall the name of the Angels learnt. 3. Point out the specific duties of the Angels.

resources.title: Jinn and Shaytan
resources.description: Theme: TAWHID | Content: 1. Jinn is another kind of supernatural creature of Allah. 2. They were created from fire, (Qur’ān 15: 27). 3. They receive revelation through Allah’s messengers (Qur’ān 46: 29 – 31. 4. Shaytan of the Jinn was created from fire. 5. Shaytan held an important position among the angels, before the creation of Adam. 6. He disobeyed Allah by refusing to prostrate before Adam as ordered by Allah. 7. Became accursed and driven out of Aljanah.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Explain that Jinn is a kind of supernatural creature of Allah. 2. say that Allah created Jinn from fire. 3. Mention the likeness and differences between human beings and Jinn. 4. Explain that Shaytan is of Jinn. 5. Explain the position of Shaytan, before the creation of Adam and why Shaytan became accursed.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads the pupils through discussion to know who jinn are, what they are created from, similarities/differe nces between them and human beings. 2. Discusses Shaytan and his link with jinn, his position among the Angels before his disobedience to Allah. 3. Explains the fate of Shaytan.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to teacher’s discussion on the topic. 2. Learn to say “Audhu-billahi- Mina-shaytanir- Rajim. 3. Identify some Shaytanic behaviours of today.
resources.resources: 1. Cardboard showing picture of a man or woman being used by Shaytan. 2. Cardboard showing how people are being manipulated by shaytan such as fighting, drinking alcohol, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Explain that jinn is a kind of supernatural creature of Allah. 2. Say that Allah created jinn from fire; 3. Mention the likeness and differences between human beings and jinn. 4. Explain that Shaytan is of jinn. 5. Explain the position of shaytan before the creation of Adam and why shaytan became accursed.

resources.title: Things that spoil salaat (Prayer).
resources.description: Theme: FIQH | Content: Things that spoil salaat: 1. Abandoning of any of the conditions’ governing performance of prayer. 2. Omission of any of the obligatory steps of prayer. 3. Omission of any emphatic sunna steps deliberately. 4. Deliberate eating or drinking. 5. Unnecessary utterances or actions deliberately done. 6. Adding deliberately any of the prayer actions or utterances, which are not required to be added. 7. Abandoning the Qibla. 8. When ablution is vitiated.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Mention things that spoil salaat. 2. Give the reasons why they spoil salaat. 3. State the need for full concentration in prayer.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains to pupils that one’s salaat can spoil. 2. Lists things that could spoil salaat as contained in the content. 3. Asks the pupils to mention those things that spoil salaat. 4. Asks the pupils to copy the things into their exercise books.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the explanation of the teacher on those things that could spoil prayers. 2. Read the things that spoil salaat. 3. Write the things as contained in their exercise books. 4. Explain how lack of concentration can be identified in prayer.
resources.resources: A cardboard containing the list of what could spoil Salaat.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Mention things that spoil salaat. 2. State the need for concentration in prayer.

resources.title: Tayammum (Dry Ablution)
resources.description: Theme: FIQH | Content: 1. Meaning of Tayammum. 2. Purpose of Tayammum. 3. Circumstances under which Tayammum is performed. 4. Practical demonstration on the performance of Tayammum. 5. What spoils Tayammum.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. State the meaning of Tayammum. 2. Explains the circumstances under which Tayammum is performed. 3. Demonstrate how Tayammum is performed. 4. Mention what spoils it.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of Tayammum. 2. Explains why Tayammum is performed e.g. when there is no water or when one cannot use water. 3. Takes pupils outside the classroom to show them how to perform Tayammum. 4. Lists the things that spoil it.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the explanation of the teacher on what Tayammum is and why it is performed. 2. Watch the practical demonstration of how Tayammum is done. 3. Perform Tayammum in turn. 4. Read what spoils Tayammum one after the other. 5. List the items with which Tayammum can be performed.
resources.resources: Sand, Stone etc.
resources.assessment: Ask the pupils to: 1. State the meaning of Tayammum. 2. Explain the circumstances under which Tayammum is performed. 3. Demonstrate how Tayammum is performed. 4. Mention what spoils it.

resources.title: Salatul-Jumuah (Friday Prayer)
resources.description: Theme: FIQH | Content: 1. Meaning of Salatul- Jumuah. 2. Differences between Salatul- Jumuah and other prayers. 3. Number of its rakat. 4. How it is performed. 5. Conditions governing its obligation. 6. Reading of Khutbah by the Imam.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Explain the meaning of Salatul-Jumuah. 2. Mention the conditions governing its obligation. 3. State when and how it is performed 4. Mention the number of its rakaat 5. State the importance of Jumuah prayer as a unify factor.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Tells the pupils that Salatul- Jumuah is an obligatory prayer, that it has two rakat. 2. Tell the pupils what differentiate it from other prayers. 3. Mention the conditions governing its obligation. 4. Quotes relevant verses from the Qur’an. 5. Tells them that anyone who could not attend Salatul-Jumuah should observe Zuhr. 6. States the importance of Jumuah prayer.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the teacher’s presentation. 2. Ask questions to clear any issue not understood. 3. Mention where your Jumuah Mosque is located. 4. Have you ever been to Jumuah Mosque? Explain how the prayer is performed. 5. Dramatize how the Imam leads the prayer.
resources.resources: Demonstration of how salatul- Jum’uah is performed.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Explain the meaning of Salatul – Jumu’ah. 2. Mention the conditions governing its obligation, show how it is performed and when. 3. State the number of its rakat. 4. State the importance of Jumuah prayer.

resources.title: Life of Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W), from his call to Prophethood to, the factors that led to Hijrah.
resources.description: Theme: SIRAH | Content: 1. Prophet Muhammad’s honesty earned him respect among people. 2. The Prophet avoided bad company and he was always in search of the truth. 3. Allah gave the Prophet the qualities of good human relation. 4. Prophet Muhammad’s search for truth led him to engaging in meditation in the cave of Hira, where he received the first revelation.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Explain why people loved and respected the Prophet before his call to Prophet hood. 2. Explain why the Prophet went to the cave ofHira and his experience when the first revelation came to him. 3. Explain the opposition of the unbelievers of Makkah to the message sent by Allah to Prophet Muhammad. 4. Recall some of the ways the Prophet and the Muslims were persecuted by the unbelievers of Makkah.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides the pupils through discussion or lecture to know that Allah gave the Prophet qualities of good human relations. 2. Recall Prophet’s judgment over the placing of Hajrul- Aswad. 3. Tells pupils how the Prophet searched for the cave of Hira for meditation, where he received the first revelation. 4. Explains how the first revelation came using Qur’an 96:1 – 5.

Students: 1. Listen attentively. 2. ask questions to clarify ideas. 3. Name the places where cave Hira and Abbaysinia are located today. 4. Identify the ways Muslims are persecuted today. 5. Mention the ways Muslims can promote the teaching of Prophet Muhammad (SAW).
resources.resources: 1. Picture of the cave of Hira. 2. Picture of the Ka’aba. 3. Pictures of Hajrul Aswad. 4. A copy of the glorious Qur’an. 5. Map of Saudi Arabia, showing Makkah, Madina, and Abbysinia (Ethiopia).

resources.title: Importance of human relation and Mutual Cooperation in Islam.
resources.description: Theme: TAHDHIB | Content: 1. Obedience to parents:-Reasons for it and the ways it can be shown Q17: 23 2. Kindness to: a. Parents b. Elders c. Fellow children d. Neighbours e. Other creatures. 3.Modesty Q 24 : 30 – 31
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Explain the reasons why they should cooperate with people such as parents, brothers and others . 2. Identify the people they should be obedient to 3. Point out an act of kindness and modesty.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the Importance of Human relation. 2. Narrates examples of punctuality, modesty and obedience. 4. Discusses the way through which obedience can be shown to them i.e. love them, be kind to them, greet them in the morning and do things that will make them happy.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher’s explanation. 2. Mention why they should be obedient to their parents, teachers, elders and leaders. 3. Demonstrate acts of kindness in a play. 4. Demonstrate act of modesty in role-play.
resources.resources: 1. Holy Qur’ān. 2. Information Technology Device etc..
